reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the webinar promotes OneCoin through a network-marketing organization, presents expanding membership as a way to create coin value, and encourages attendees to join the mining program. Speakers also pitch the opportunity with a claim that customers can position themselves for “a massive profit” and predictions of substantial growth. The supplied material does not establish an individual loss or completed payout.

citations.quote: bring one coin in a network marketing concept
the more we are, the more valuable the product becomes, and the more interesting and becomes for all of us.
that marketing engine that is everyone on this call
start mining their coins and position themselves for a massive profit.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present appreciation as a certainty. The discussion expressly warns that rapid growth can create a bubble and says viewers should not expect the price to skyrocket. It also distinguishes practical use from speculation, stating that the coin can succeed only if people use it, while the speaker's main interest is not investing or speculation. That is risk-aware financial commentary and conditional forecasting, not a guaranteed-return pitch. The presence of ambitious projections does not erase the explicit uncertainty and caution surrounding them.

citations.quote: we should not expect the price skyrocket too high. It is also a bad thing and actually can lead to volatility and it falls down.
my main interest and I'm extremely honest to you is not the investing, the speculation of the coin.
This coin can only be successful if you, in 1, 2, 3 years use this coin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution selects the promotional language while omitting the qualifications. Calling the format network marketing does not establish that every statement is a deceptive solicitation, and the phrase about a marketing engine describes participation in distribution, not a promised payout. Even “massive profit” is reported as a customer’s belief about potential, while the presentation itself warns against expecting a price spike.

citations.quote: bring one coin in a network marketing concept
that marketing engine that is everyone on this call
position themselves for a massive profit
we should not expect the price skyrocket too high

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings about volatility do not neutralize the central promotion. The speaker still frames network growth as creating value and presents mining as a route to potential profit. Saying the coin should be used does not make the financial opportunity merely educational; it links participation, future value, and the audience's actions.

opening.argument: This is substantially a cryptocurrency education and product demonstration. The presentation explains how Bitcoin began, how transactions and mining work, why difficulty changes, and how a blockchain is supposed to record coins. It also gives a hypothetical example of sending coins internationally and describes a possible future card use. Explaining an emerging technology and comparing its design with Bitcoin is not, by itself, scam content. The focus is on concepts, mechanics, and proposed utility rather than documenting a completed payout or a victim’s loss.

citations.quote: In 2009, in January, they mined, created the 50 first Bitcoin, and this is actually how it all started.
if you send coins takes less than 10 minutes
we are the first crypto currency with an audited blockchain
one coin is a very very similar concept actually technicly. Like Bitcoin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the setting as dispositive, but a company webinar can contain genuine technical education. The supplied quotations do not show a completed transaction, a guaranteed return, or a specific enrollment demand. Describing network marketing and explaining how cryptocurrency might gain value are topics under discussion; they do not establish that the presentation's primary function was a deceptive scam mechanism.

citations.quote: bring one coin in a network marketing concept
the more we are, the more valuable the product becomes, and the more interesting and becomes for all of us.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical material is embedded in a launch presentation, not detached instruction. The explanation repeatedly turns mechanics into a reason to participate, including the claim that members create the coins and the proposal to make the coin liquid through a card network. Educational detail can make a solicitation more persuasive; it does not change the promotional purpose.

citations.quote: all coins will be created by you, will be distributed to you
this is something that is the goal of our company to make one coin accessible for everyone to make one coin liquid
we will do a tour with lots of cities and with lots of people from Europe and Asia in order to help a lot of people with the business concepts

opening.argument: The strongest grounded reading is an ordinary customer-facing cryptocurrency and mining promotion, with important scam mechanisms left unestablished. The speaker describes a customer who can participate without becoming an affiliate or building a team, and the slides frame mining as a process involving tokens, pools, and coins. The supplied material does not establish a required deposit, a guaranteed return, a completed payout, or a request for credentials. Potential utility and future liquidity are presented as business goals, not as proof that viewers will receive money.

citations.quote: someone can get involved just at the customer level without having to become an independent marketing affiliate without having to build a team
start mining their coins and position themselves for a massive profit
the goal of our company to make one coin accessible for everyone to make one coin liquid

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited evidence does not show an ordinary retail purchase, but it also does not show the missing scam mechanism the prosecution needs. The customer-level description expressly separates use from team-building, and the words “potential profit” do not establish a guarantee. A branded mining slide and optimistic business claims are insufficient to prove that money was taken or that returns were promised.

citations.quote: without having to become an independent marketing affiliate without having to build a team
a massive profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The customer-level wording does not make the opportunity ordinary commerce when the same presentation promotes mining and ties value to expanding participation. “Potential” softens the promise but still markets financial upside, while the mining slide directly asks how to join the miner. The absence of a shown payout is not evidence that the promotion was legitimate.
